scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Con The Human League a la cabeza, el auge de 1981-1982: los sintetizadores baratos (el Wasp), las cajas de ritmos Linn y las baterías Simmons democratizan la electrónica, al punto de que el sindicato de músicos propone racionarlos. Instrumento andrógino frente a la guitarra fálica, refugio para los adolescentes que se sentían distintos. Soft Cell lleva la sordidez neoyorquina de Suicide a Leeds («Tainted Love», «Bedsitter», Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret); Japan, máscaras de dandi de Catford, pasa del glam desfasado a la belleza escultural de «Ghosts»; OMD, Pete Shelley («Homosapien»), y Depeche Mode, de chicos inocentes de Basildon en Mute a la política y el sadomasoquismo de «Everything Counts» y «Master and Servant». Hacia 1983 el diluvio de grupos mediocres provoca la reacción y vuelven las guitarras.

podcast.title: Devotional Tour Behavior and Arrest (1993)
podcast.body: During the Devotional Tour, Martin Gore reportedly drank vast amounts of beer and often stripped naked. He relied on very strong sleeping pills to get any sleep. On November 3, 1993, he was arrested in Denver for playing loud music in his hotel room at 4 AM and spent the night in jail. "Martin Gore would allegedly drink vast amounts of beer and then strip naked."

podcast.title: Panic Attacks and Seizures (1993)
podcast.body: Martin Gore experienced severe panic attacks, leading him to believe he was dying, and he really should have been taking it easy. In November 1993, ahead of five nights at the Great Western Forum in Los Angeles, he suffered a grand mal seizure during a business meeting at the Sunset Marquis Hotel. This was his second such attack, attributed to stress, alcohol, and drugs, in addition to numerous minor panic attacks. "Then came a grand mall seizure in the middle of a business meeting at the Sunset Marquis Hotel in Los Angeles in November 1993, a head of five nights at the Great Western Forum."

podcast.title: Chief Songwriter for Depeche Mode
podcast.body: Martin Gore has been the primary songwriter for virtually all of Depeche Mode's material, consistently credited on albums from A Broken Frame in 1982 to the present day. "The chief songwriter for 99% of Depeche Mode's existence has been Martin Gore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Consideration of a Solo Career
podcast.body: During the period of uncertainty surrounding Depeche Mode's future and Dave Gahan's addiction, Martin Gore came very close to initiating a solo career. There were discussions that the album Ultra might even become his first solo record, with support from Andy Fletcher. Although he eventually released solo work later, this period marked a serious consideration of branching out on his own. "Martin Gorko estuvo a punto de arrancar una carrera en solitario prácticamente desde el inicio de la banda que hoy si que la tenemos tenemos algunos trabajos en Martin Gorko."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Increased Role Post-Wilder's Departure
podcast.body: Following Alan Wilder's departure from Depeche Mode, Martin Gore stepped into a more prominent and comprehensive creative role within the band. He became "completely euphoric," engaging more deeply in composing, recording, and producing the band's music, particularly evident in the creation of Ultra. This shift allowed his talent to shine more brightly, shaping the band's new sound. "Vemos un martingor completamente pletórico, componiendo, grabando, produciendo."

podcast.title: Influenced by Industrial Bands
podcast.body: As the songwriter for Depeche Mode, Martin Gore privately listened to aggressive industrial acts such as Fad Gadget (known for using power drills), Test Department (known for performances in quarries and car factories), and Einstürzende Neubauten. This exposure led him to incorporate industrial elements into Depeche Mode's music as he gained more control. "But if you would ask songwriter Martin Gore, who he listened to in his spare time, he would have listed names like Fad Gadget, the group that liked to use black and decker power drills in their music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sobriety and Continued Music Career (Late 1990s-Present)
podcast.body: Martin Gore achieved sobriety midway through the recording of the "Ultra" album, which eased the rest of the recording process, particularly the vocal tracks. He continues to record and tour with Dave Gahan, maintaining a sober lifestyle. "Halfway through the recording of this record, Dave got clean and sober."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Songwriting Dominance and Personal Challenges (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Martin Gore became the sole songwriter for Depeche Mode, which created tension with Alan Wilder. He claimed to be autistic and indulged heavily in partying and drinking, often withdrawing into video games like "Sonic the Hedgehog." Becoming a father for the first time in June 1991 added further stress. "He wanted to contribute more as a songwriter, but that had pretty much become the sole domain of Martin Gore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Struggles with Alcoholism and Personal Problems (Mid-1990s)
podcast.body: In the mid-1990s, concurrent with the band's lowest point, Martin Gore faced significant personal challenges, including problems with alcoholism and intense sentimental issues. These struggles put him in a very difficult period of his life and contributed to the overall tension within Depeche Mode. His emotional state, marked by sadness, aggression, and exhaustion from sleeplessness and relationship conflicts, is palpably present in the Ultra album. "Martin Gorko muchos problemas al colismo pero también con muchos problemas sentimentales, él estaba en un momento muy malo de su vida."

xref.title: Joining Depeche Mode and Creative Frustration (1982-1991)
xref.body: Alan Wilder was the last to join Depeche Mode in 1982, serving as a synth player and programmer. By 1991, he grew frustrated as songwriting became almost exclusively Martin Gore's domain, limiting his creative contributions. "He was the last person to join Depeche Mode, signing on in 1982 as a synth player and programmer."

xref.title: Martin Gore Arrested in Denver (November 4, 1993)
xref.body: On November 4, 1993, Martin Gore was arrested at the Weston Hotel in Denver. The arrest happened after he refused to turn down his stereo at 4 in the morning following complaints about the noise. "November 4, 1993. Martin Gore was arrested at the Weston Hotel in Denver after refusing to turn down the stereo at 4 in the morning."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Overdose and Heart Attack in New Orleans (October 8, 1993)
xref.body: In New Orleans, Dave Gahan overdosed between the main set and the encore, suffering a heart attack that required paramedics to rush him to the hospital, leading Martin Gore to perform a solo song for the encore. Dave recalled hearing the song "Death's Door" in the background during this near-fatal incident. "At the end of the gig, I couldn't go back for the encore."

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Near-Death Experience and Recovery (1995-1996)
xref.body: From late spring 1995 through to a brief clinical death in 1996, Dave Gahan's life was consumed by heroin addiction, costing $3,000 daily, leading to extreme dissociation, conversations with stuffed animals (including a Bugs Bunny doll), and two suicide attempts. On May 27, 1996, after an attempt to record with Martin Gore, Gahan injected cocaine and heroin at the Sunset Marquis Hotel in Hollywood, leading to full cardiac arrest and two minutes of clinical death. He recalled a vision of his wife screaming for him to return and a voice stating, "This is wrong, you don't get to decide." His recovery began after summer 1996, largely influenced by the threat of green card revocation from the American government if he didn't enter rehab and remain sober. He has been sober since June 6, 1996, now runs four times a week, lives in New York's West Village, and is married to Jennifer, his third wife. "He was for all intents and purposes clinically dead for two full minutes. He now says he remembers the vision of his wife screaming at him to come back to this plane."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Long-Term Recovery and Current Status (1997-Present)
xref.body: Depeche Mode eventually overcame the tumultuous period between 1991 and 1997. Dave Gahan and Martin Gore are now sober, and Alan Wilder is living a quiet life. While Andy Fletcher died in 2022, Martin Gore and Dave Gahan continue to record and tour together, showing intent to move forward almost 50 years after the band's formation. "The good news is that the Pesh mode eventually came out on the other side of all things that happened between 1991 and 1997."

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Quiet Demeanor
xref.body: Andy Fletcher was known as the "quiet one" in Depeche Mode, content to let Dave Gahan and Martin Gore handle most of the speaking during interviews. "Andy was the quiet one in Depeche Mode."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Members' Current Residences
xref.body: Martin Gore resides in Santa Barbara, California, where his ex-wife owns a spa. Dave Gahan lives in New York, and Andrew Fletcher has his home in the Maidstone area of London. "So we got Martin living in California. There's Dave in New York and Andrew in London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Blend of Technopop and Industrial
xref.body: Depeche Mode was positioned as a band "caught right in the middle" of the Technopop and industrial scenes, known for being polite and innocuous Technopop while their songwriter, Martin Gore, was influenced by aggressive industrial acts. This blend led to the incorporation of industrial elements into their music. "Depeche Mode is a great example. They were caught right in the middle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Complexity of "Behind the Wheel" ISRC Numbers
xref.body: Depeche Mode's song "Behind the Wheel" from *Music for the Masses* highlights the ISRC system's challenges, with countless remixes, re-releases on various labels and territories, and different formats (vinyl, CD, digital files), making it nearly impossible to track all unique identifiers, even for band member Martin Gore by 2003. "And even Martin Gore has no clue how many times this song has been remixed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Decadent Tour Staff and Incidents
xref.body: The "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour employed approximately 100 individuals, including a dedicated full-time psychiatrist and a staff member specifically tasked with procuring drugs. During this tour, several band members experienced severe issues: Martin Gore suffered two grand mal seizures and numerous panic attacks, Andrew Fletcher endured a mental breakdown so severe that doctors initially suspected a brain tumor, and keyboardist Alan Wilder ultimately quit the band. "The tour employed a hundred people, including a full-time psychiatrist and a guy whose job it was to buy drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dominant Songwriting Role
xref.body: Martin Gore has consistently been the chief songwriter for almost all of Depeche Mode's material since 1982's A Broken Frame, continuing to the present. "If you care to check the credits on pretty much every album from a broken frame in 1982 to the present, you'll see that it's been pretty much all about Martin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dressing Room Arrangements on Tour
xref.body: On the road, Martin Gore and Andrew Fletcher share a dressing room, while Dave Gahan has his own. This arrangement is primarily attributed to Dave's need to avoid the temptations of backstage life. "When they're on the road, Martin and Andrew share a dressing room. Dave gets his own. That always more to Dave's need to be away from the temptations of backstage life than anything else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early 90s Struggles
xref.body: In the early 1990s, Depeche Mode was in a "very bad place" largely due to extensive drug and alcohol use. Martin Gore suffered severe seizures, leading doctors to suspect a brain tumor. Andy Fletcher (Fletch) experienced debilitating panic attacks, and keyboardist Alan Wilder quit the band due to the stress. Singer Dave Gahan was heavily addicted to heroin and cocaine. "In the early 90s, Depeche Mode was in a very bad place. Thanks to lots and lots and lots of drugs and alcohol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Gasconi – Andy Fletcher's London Italian Restaurant
xref.body: Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode, along with his wife Grania, opened an Italian restaurant called Gasconi in the mid-1990s in the St. John's Wood area of London, near Abbey Road recording studios and Violet Hill. The restaurant, located at one Blenheim Terrace, was intended as a distraction for Andy due to the adverse effects of Depeche Mode's extensive touring, which had caused him to miss part of a tour previously. It became a pilgrimage site for Depeche Mode fans, and Martin Gore, the band's songwriter, was a frequent visitor. Andy eventually sold his stake in Gasconi to focus on his record label, Toast Hawaii, and occasional DJ gigs. "Gasconi was supposed to be something that could distract him between Depeche Mode projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Martin Gore (Depeche Mode)
xref.body: Martin Gore, the songwriter for Depeche Mode, listed Einstürzende Neubauten among the industrial bands he listened to in his spare time, indicating their significant influence on his musical development and later work with Depeche Mode. "And of course, Einstein's Andy Neubaden. This aggressive approach to music really appealed to Martin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Martin Gore Becomes Chief Songwriter
xref.body: Following Vince Clarke's departure on December 1, 1981, Martin Gore, formerly a bank clerk, assumed the role of Depeche Mode's chief songwriter. Since then, he has written approximately 99.9% of the band's material, a contribution credited with helping Depeche Mode become one of the biggest new rock bands globally. "Since that day, Vince Clark left the band, Martin has written 99.9% of Depeche Mode's material."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Martin Gore's Binge Drinking (Hamburg, Germany)
xref.body: Martin Gore was known for severe binge drinking, with one account stating he once consumed 67 pints of lager in a single 11-hour sitting in Hamburg, Germany. This extreme feat for a man who is five feet eight inches tall required many trips to the bathroom. "One report says that Martin Gore once drank 67 pints of logger in a single sitting in Hamburg, Germany."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Martin Gore's Real Estate Investments
xref.body: Martin Gore, in addition to being the group's chief songwriter, is a successful real estate investor, with one commercial property in London's revitalized Docklands District. This property generates over a quarter of a million pounds in rent annually, and ironically, one of its tenants is a branch of the bank where Gore worked as a teller in the late 1970s. "One of his commercial properties is in the revitalized Docklands District of London. It generates more than a quarter of a million pounds in rent every year. And in a delicious piece of irony, one of the tenants is a branch of the bank where Martin used to work as a teller in the late 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Martin Gore's Seizures
xref.body: During the 1993-94 Devotional Tour, Martin Gore experienced seizures, which were attributed to his heavy alcohol and drug use, combined with incessant partying. "Martin Gore ended up suffering from seizures brought on by alcohol drugs and incessant partying."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Model, Writer, Spiritualist, Musician
xref.body: Andrea Hogan, a German-born musician, was a former model who wrote horror movies, supported the Goth scene, and was a poet and pagan spiritualist. She worked under various names, including Hügellands Roondance, exploring genres from ambient and electronic to rock, industrial, and black metal. She was also friends with musicians like Martin Gore of Depeche Mode. "Andrea was a former model who wrote horror movies and supported the Goth scene. She was a poet and pagan spiritualist. She was also a musician who worked under a variety of names and a variety of genres, ranging from ambient and electronic to rock industrial and even black metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Tour Health Crisis (Devotional Tour Aftermath)
xref.body: The aftermath of the Devotional Tour saw several band members facing severe health issues: Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney and gall stones during the South African leg; Andrew Fletcher nearly suffered a nervous breakdown and left the tour for treatment after his sister died of stomach cancer; Martin Gore experienced a grand mal seizure during a business meeting due to excessive drugs and alcohol; and Dave Gahan's severe drug use led to extreme weight loss (under 100 pounds) and an incident where he bit a journalist on the neck. "During the South African leg, Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney stones and then gall stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Religious Background of Members
xref.body: Founding members Andrew Fletcher and Vince Clark were born-again Christians as teenagers, and their singing of hymns and devotional songs initially attracted Martin Gore and Dave Gahan, who were described as "essentially pagan unbelievers." Spiritually, Gore and Gahan have since "lapsed." "Andrew Fletcher and founding member Vince Clark were born again Christians as teenagers. Martin Gore and Dave Gahan, both essentially pagan unbelievers, were drawn to Andrew and Vince because they liked the hymns and devotional songs that they had heard Andrew and Vince sing."

xref.title: Unconventional Performance Venues
xref.body: Test Department was a group known for staging performances in unusual and industrial locations such as quarries and car factories, reflecting an aggressive approach to music that appealed to Martin Gore of Depeche Mode. "Then there was Test Department, a group we liked to stage performances in places like quarries and car factories."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Use of Power Drills in Music
xref.body: Fad Gadget was known for incorporating Black & Decker power drills into their music, an aggressive and unconventional approach that appealed to and influenced artists like Martin Gore of Depeche Mode. "Fad Gadget, the group that liked to use black and decker power drills in their music."
